newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, IMF welcomes BI move.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, IMF welcomes BI move.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in moderate early trading on Friday, a day after it was allowed to float, recovering from an overnight dip in London to 2,815, dealers said.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) welcomed the float, saying the move would allow the country's economy to continue its recent impressive performance.

"In present circumstances, a floating exchange rate will enhance the effectiveness of macroeconomic policies aimed at sustaining high rates of growth with financial stability," said Stanley Fischer, acting managing director of the IMF.

Dealers said offshore sentiment appeared to be positive on the rupiah, with buying orders seen entering the market and capping the dollar at the 2,800 level. "But our main worry is local corporates who are eager to hedge now despite the tight rupiah conditions," one dealer said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,790/2,800 at 0235 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,770/90. The rupiah strengthened to a high of 2,770 but sustained local buying interest pushed the dollar up again.
Dealers said offshore operators were not as aggressive as before since there was no longer any speculative push to test the intervention band.
Bank Indonesia announced on Thursday it was immediately ending its system of managing exchange rates through the use of an intervention band, effectively floating the rupiah.

"Some offshores are trying to lock in the attractive yield. But nervous local corporates have dented any possible rupiah recovery," another said, adding that it would take some days for the market to fully digest the new exchange rate system.

Central bank intervention on Wednesday of some $500 million, which was maturing on Friday, together with a tight short-term monetary policy, sent overnight rates to a record high of 125 percent before they eased slightly to 110 percent.
Swap rates were driven up by the tight liquidity in the money market, with overnight swap soaring to a high of 26/27 points, equivalent to 360 percent interest.
Dealers said the dollar was also supported by operators who were caught short on dollars on Thursday and were trying to square their positions on Friday.
Fischer called Indonesia's decision timely and said it came partly in response to turbulence on regional currency markets.
He said floating the rupiah was "in line with Bank Indonesia's steady progress toward greater exchange rate flexibility, particularly over the last two years."

"The floating of the rupiah, in combination with Indonesia's strong fundamentals, supported by prudent fiscal and monetary policies, will allow its economy to continue its impressive economic performance of the last several years," Fischer said in a statement.
